introduction.en: Which Blue Lock character do your voluntary tabletop choices bring to mind? Imagine friends designing a harmless football game with paper and counters: observing a replay, offering play, starting simply, choosing a role, clarifying a plan, keeping a personal routine or choosing the tempo. This independent anime fan edition has 21 original situations and seven complete public guides before you start. No physical exercise, sporting tryout, injury story or episode knowledge is required.
introduction.zh: 自愿桌面选择会让你想到《蓝色监狱》的哪位人物？想象朋友用纸和棋子设计无害足球游戏：看回放、提玩趣、简单开始、选角色、澄清计划、留个人惯例或选节奏。本独立动画同人版有21原创情境和七份开测前可读全文，不需身体锻炼、选拔、伤病故事或剧情知识。

instructions.en: Think about a small optional tabletop game you would enjoy now. Choose one of four responses in every situation, even if none fits perfectly. There is no correct answer or ranking of strength, intelligence or worth. A character absent from an item is not rejected. Finish all 21 choices before counts appear; every highest tie receives a complete guide.
instructions.zh: 想象现在愿玩的可选桌面小游戏，每情境四选一，即使都不完美。无正确答案，不排名力量、智力、价值；当题没出现者不算被拒绝。21题选完才出次数，每个最高并列都有全文。

label.en: Watch one sample turn and revise my idea of how the pieces connect.

label.en: Try a playful counter movement everyone agrees is part of the game.
label.zh: 试大家同意属于游戏的趣味棋子走法。

label.en: Begin with one simple move instead of a whole elaborate sequence.
label.zh: 从一个简单走步开始，不先作复杂整套。

label.en: Choose a contribution, with room to switch if another part interests me.

prompt.en: The paper pitch has room for a new optional rule. What appeals most?

label.en: Invent a lighthearted variation and ask if the group wants to try it.

label.en: Test the shortest version of the rule before adding detail.
label.zh: 加细节前先试最简版规则。

label.en: Take whichever agreed role I currently want to explore.
label.zh: 接现在想探索、已约好的角色。

label.en: Write a precise example so everybody knows what the new rule means.
label.zh: 写精确例子，让大家知新规则何意。

prompt.en: A complicated token sequence makes the homemade game hard to start. What would you prefer?

label.en: Try a single easy turn and build from what actually works.
label.zh: 试一个简单回合，从真可用处往下做。

label.en: Switch to another voluntary contribution that fits my current interest.
label.zh: 换另个合当前兴趣的自愿贡献。

label.en: Clarify the sequence’s steps before the group uses it.

label.en: Choose one I want now and stay free to change by agreement later.
label.zh: 选现在想做的，留以后约好再换的自由。

label.en: Agree exactly what the selected role involves before starting.

label.en: Arrange my own counters in a repeatable order I like.
label.zh: 按自己喜欢、可重复顺序摆自己的棋子。

label.en: Choose a comfortable pace rather than follow somebody else’s fastest turn.
label.zh: 选舒服节奏，不跟别人的最快回合。

prompt.en: Two friends understand a homemade passing rule differently. What would you enjoy?
prompt.zh: 两朋友对自编传棋子规则理解不同，你喜欢什么？

label.en: Make a clear example and agree which interpretation to use.
label.zh: 作清楚示例，约用哪种解释。

label.en: Keep a consistent personal preparation step while the group decides.
label.zh: 大家决定时，保持自己的固定准备步。

label.en: Allow enough pause between turns for the chosen pace to feel comfortable.
label.zh: 回合间容许够暂停，让选定节奏舒服。

label.en: Observe both sample moves and update my proposed arrangement.
label.zh: 看两种示例走法，再改建议布局。

prompt.en: You are setting out your own pieces for the optional paper-pitch game. What would you prefer?
prompt.zh: 为可选纸球场游戏摆自己的棋子，你更愿意怎样做？

label.en: Use a neat personal routine that does not impose an order on anyone else.
label.zh: 用整齐个人惯例，不把顺序强加别人。

label.en: Set a pace that lets me enjoy placing the pieces.
label.zh: 定能享受摆棋子的节奏。

label.en: Look at the layout and revise one connection I had assumed.
label.zh: 看布局，改一处原本默认的连接。

label.en: Add a harmless playful detail if the group wants it.
label.zh: 若大家愿意，添一项无害趣味细节。

prompt.en: Friends suggest playing the tabletop round as fast as possible. What appeals most?
prompt.zh: 朋友建议桌面这一轮尽快玩，什么最吸引你？

label.en: Agree a tempo I actually want, including pauses or passing my turn.
label.zh: 约自己真想的节奏，含暂停或略过回合。

label.en: Watch how one round unfolds before changing my approach.
label.zh: 先看一轮怎样展开，再改方法。

label.en: Try a playful variation that is enjoyable without racing.
label.zh: 试不竞速也有趣的变式。

label.en: Start with a short, simple turn rather than speed up everything.
label.zh: 从简短回合开始，不把所有都加速。

prompt.en: A replay with counters reveals a gap in your first paper-pitch idea. What would you enjoy?
prompt.zh: 用棋子回放发现首个纸球场点子有缺口，你喜欢什么？

label.en: Redraw one connection based on what the replay actually shows.
label.zh: 依回放实际所示，重画一个连接。

label.en: Explore an agreed unexpected move for the fun of trying it.
label.zh: 为尝试乐趣，探索约好的意外走法。

label.en: Reduce the idea to a small move that can be tested now.
label.zh: 把点子缩成现在可试的小走步。

label.en: Choose a different part of the project if it now interests me more.
label.zh: 若更感兴趣，就选项目另一部分。

prompt.en: The group wants a cheerful twist for its invented tabletop match. What would you prefer?
prompt.zh: 小组想给虚构桌面比赛添开心变化，你更愿意怎样做？

label.en: Suggest a surprising but agreed counter pattern with no target for ridicule.
label.zh: 提惊喜、经同意的棋子图样，不拿谁嘲笑。

label.en: Try the least complicated version so we can begin playing.
label.zh: 试最不复杂版，让大家能开玩。

label.en: Explore a different voluntary role for this round.
label.zh: 这轮探索不同自愿角色。

label.en: Give the twist a clear definition before it becomes a shared rule.
label.zh: 成为共同规则前，给变化清楚定义。

prompt.en: Only a few minutes are available for the paper game today. What appeals most?
prompt.zh: 今天纸游戏只剩几分钟，什么最吸引你？

label.en: Enjoy one simple sequence rather than wait for a perfect full match.
label.zh: 享受一个简单序列，不等完美全场。

label.en: Pick the contribution I want for this short session.
label.zh: 给短活动选自己想作的贡献。

label.en: Agree the exact stopping point so the short round is clear.
label.zh: 约准确终点，让短轮清楚。

label.en: Use my usual small setup order to get my pieces ready.
label.zh: 用惯常小准备顺序，把自己棋子备好。

prompt.en: You have already tried arranging counters and could now write rules. What would you enjoy?
prompt.zh: 已试摆棋子，现在能写规则，你喜欢什么？

label.en: Change contribution because the new part interests me, without owing anyone a fixed role.
label.zh: 因新部分有兴趣而换贡献，不欠谁固定角色。

label.en: Agree a clear example of what the written rule should cover.
label.zh: 约书面规则涵盖什么的清楚例子。

label.en: Keep a repeatable personal way of organising my materials.
label.zh: 保持自己组织材料的可重复方法。

label.en: Choose a tempo that makes the change comfortable.
label.zh: 选让切换舒服的节奏。

prompt.en: A new counter rule needs an example before friends can use it. What appeals most?
prompt.zh: 新棋子规则需示例才好用，什么最吸引你？

label.en: Write the steps precisely and invite the group to check them.
label.zh: 精确写步骤，邀小组核对。

label.en: Set out my own example pieces using a familiar routine.
label.zh: 按熟悉惯例，摆自己的示例棋子。

label.en: Give people time to follow the example without racing to finish.
label.zh: 给时间跟示例，不抢完成。

label.en: Watch a trial turn and revise what the example leaves unclear.
label.zh: 看试走回合，改示例不清处。

prompt.en: Your own materials keep getting mixed during the voluntary tabletop session. What would you prefer?
prompt.zh: 自愿桌面活动中，自己的材料总混起来，你更愿意怎样做？

label.en: Create a small personal place-and-reset routine that others do not have to copy.
label.zh: 作个人放置、复位小惯例，别人不必照搬。

label.en: Pause long enough to reset at a pace I choose.
label.zh: 按自己选节奏，暂停够久再复位。

label.en: Observe which arrangement actually causes the confusion and change it.
label.zh: 观察哪布局真造成混淆，再改它。

label.en: Try a playful label system if everyone enjoys the idea.
label.zh: 若大家喜欢，试趣味标签系统。

prompt.en: The next round can include longer pauses or quicker token turns. What would you enjoy?
prompt.zh: 下一轮可长暂停或快走棋子，你喜欢什么？

label.en: Choose the tempo I want rather than treat quickness as a requirement.
label.zh: 选想要的节奏，不把快当要求。

label.en: Watch one turn at each tempo and update my layout idea.
label.zh: 各节奏看一回合，改布局点子。

label.en: Invent a harmless optional pattern that works at either pace.
label.zh: 编两节奏都可用的无害可选图样。

label.en: Keep just one easy move so the round stays approachable.
label.zh: 只留一个易走步，让这轮好加入。

prompt.en: A counter replay makes an earlier plan look less useful. What appeals most?
prompt.zh: 棋子回放让早先计划显得没用，你最喜欢什么？

label.en: Use the new observation to revise the plan without defending every old detail.
label.zh: 用新观察改计划，不替每个旧细节辩护。

label.en: Try a lighthearted alternative the group agrees to explore.
label.zh: 试小组同意探索的轻松替代。

label.en: Return to one workable move and see what follows.
label.zh: 回到一个可用走步，看后续怎样。

label.en: Take another agreed role if that is what I want now.
label.zh: 若现在想如此，就接另一约好角色。

prompt.en: The optional paper game has begun to feel repetitive. What would you prefer?
prompt.zh: 可选纸游戏开始重复，你更愿意怎样做？

label.en: Offer an imaginative counter variation that everyone can decline.
label.zh: 提有想象的棋子变式，人人可拒绝。

label.en: Try a single fresh move without building a large new system.
label.zh: 试一个新走步，不另造大系统。

label.en: Choose another part of the session that interests me.
label.zh: 选活动里另一感兴趣部分。

label.en: Clarify which rule can change and which one the group wants to keep.
label.zh: 澄清哪条可变、哪条大家想留。

prompt.en: Friends have designed an impressive tabletop sequence that takes too long to explain. What appeals most?
prompt.zh: 朋友设计精彩桌面序列，却要解释很久，什么最吸引你？

label.en: Test one small part now rather than postpone all the enjoyment.
label.zh: 现在试一小部分，不推迟全部乐趣。

label.en: Choose whether I want to explain, arrange or simply watch this time.
label.zh: 选这次想解释、摆放或只看。

label.en: Define one short example that the group can check.
label.zh: 定义一个小组可核的短示例。

label.en: Prepare my own pieces in the familiar order that suits me.
label.zh: 按合自己的熟悉顺序，备自己的棋子。

prompt.en: People expect you to repeat the same role at the next paper-pitch session. What would you enjoy?
prompt.zh: 大家期待下次纸球场活动还做同角色，你喜欢什么？

label.en: Choose again, agreeing any change instead of assuming the role is permanent.
label.zh: 重新选、约好变化，不默认角色永久。

label.en: Set out what the next agreed role includes in precise terms.
label.zh: 精确写下次约好角色含什么。

label.en: Keep one personal preparation habit regardless of which role I choose.
label.zh: 无论选哪角色，都留一个个人准备习惯。

label.en: Decide how quickly I want to move through the new session.
label.zh: 决定想用多快节奏进行新活动。

prompt.en: A written rule and a sample counter move do not quite agree. What would you prefer?
prompt.zh: 书面规则与棋子示例不太一致，你更愿意怎样做？

label.en: Compare them carefully and agree a precise correction.
label.zh: 仔细比较，约一项准确修正。

label.en: Reset my own materials in a consistent order while we decide.
label.zh: 决定时，用一致顺序复位自己的材料。

label.en: Allow a pause rather than rush people through the mismatch.
label.zh: 容许暂停，不催人草草过差异。

label.en: Observe another trial and revise my interpretation of the layout.
label.zh: 再看一试走，改对布局的解释。

prompt.en: The homemade game is ending, and you are putting away your own counters. What appeals most?
prompt.zh: 自编游戏结束，正收自己的棋子，什么最吸引你？

label.en: Use my chosen tidy routine without setting a standard for everyone else.
label.zh: 用自选整理惯例，不给所有人定标准。

label.en: Close the session at a comfortable pace with room to pause.
label.zh: 按舒服节奏收尾，留暂停空间。

label.en: Notice one layout detail worth revising next time.
label.zh: 注意一处下次值得改的布局细节。

label.en: Keep one optional playful idea for another session.
label.zh: 留一个可选玩趣点子待后续活动。

prompt.en: Friends ask what tempo you would want for another voluntary tabletop round. What would you enjoy?
prompt.zh: 朋友问下次自愿桌面一轮想用何节奏，你喜欢什么？

label.en: Choose it afresh, including slower play, pauses or sitting the round out.
label.zh: 重新选，含慢玩、暂停或这轮不参加。

label.en: Watch a sample before deciding how to revise my approach.
label.zh: 决定怎样改方法前，看一个示例。

label.en: Try a consensual imaginative move instead of making speed the focus.
label.zh: 试经同意的想象走法，不把速度当重点。

label.en: Begin with a small straightforward sequence and see if I want more.
label.zh: 先作小而直接序列，看是否还想继续。

title.en: Isagi’s selected angle

paragraphs.en: Isagi is one of seven anime characters selected for this independent fan edition. His angle here is observing a tabletop turn and revising a paper layout. It does not score intelligence, spatial ability, learning speed or an ability to win at football. A small revision is simply one enjoyable way to explore how an invented game works without treating another player as an obstacle to destroy.
paragraphs.zh: 洁世一是本独立同人版选定七动画人物之一，角度是观察桌面回合、修改纸布局，不评智力、空间能力、学习速度或足球获胜能力。小修改只是探索自编游戏怎样运作的乐趣，不把别人当须摧毁的障碍。

title.en: A connection changes after a replay

paragraphs.en: You thought two counters could connect easily, but a sample turn shows that the paper rule leaves a gap. You redraw one line and try again with the group’s agreement. The useful observation is specific to this little layout. It does not prove that you read real opponents accurately, copy people successfully or need to dismantle your identity whenever a plan stops working.
paragraphs.zh: 原以为两棋子易连接，示例却显示纸规则有缺口。你经大家同意重画一线、再试。有用观察只关这小布局，不证明看穿真人对手、成功模仿或每次计划失效都需推翻自我。

title.en: Observation beside six other contributions

paragraphs.en: Bachira tries a playful variation, Nagi starts with a simple move and Reo chooses a different contribution. Rin clarifies the plan, Barou uses a personal routine and Chigiri chooses the tempo. Isagi’s selected angle updates the map after watching. These contributions can coexist without ranking intelligence or ambition. Tied guides offer several readings of your choices, not evidence of competing selves or a hidden talent profile.
paragraphs.zh: 蜂乐试趣味变化，凪从简单走步开始，玲王选不同贡献；凛澄清计划，马狼用个人惯例，千切选节奏。洁的角度看后改图。可共存，不排智力、野心；并列给多读法，不证明自我冲突、隐藏天赋。

title.en: A useful revision does not require endless analysis
title.zh: 有用修改不需无尽分析

paragraphs.en: It can be tempting to keep replaying a small turn instead of enjoying the next one. Decide whether the observation changes anything the group wants to try now, and leave the rest for later. Your count cannot establish exceptional perception or relentless competitiveness. A lower count does not imply poor awareness, weak reasoning or an inability to learn, and an invented game is not a model of every real situation.
paragraphs.zh: 反复回放小回合可能替代继续玩。可决定观察是否影响现在想试的，其他留后。次数不确立超强观察、无休竞争；低计数不表示觉察差、推理弱、不会学，虚构游戏也不代表所有现实。

title.en: Try one observation and one reversible change
title.zh: 试一次观察与可改回变化

paragraphs.en: In a voluntary paper game, watch one sample turn and note one concrete connection that could be clearer. Ask the group whether to test a small revision, then compare how the two layouts play. Keep either or neither. You are checking a design choice, not measuring your brain, proving superiority over friends or receiving advice about competitive sport, professional performance or major life decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 自愿纸游戏中，看一示例、记一个可更清楚连接，问大家是否试小改，再比两布局玩法。可留任一或都不留。这核设计，不测大脑、不证明优于朋友、不指导竞技、职业表现或重大决定。

title.en: Bachira’s selected angle

paragraphs.en: Bachira’s selected angle is a playful variation in a harmless tabletop game, offered so everyone can freely accept or decline. It is not a measure of eccentricity, intuition, loneliness or a need for approval. You do not need an unusual identity to enjoy moving paper counters differently, and nobody’s discomfort has to become the entertainment. The match makes no claim about your football technique or creative talent.
paragraphs.zh: 蜂乐角度是无害桌游的趣味变式，人人能自由接受或拒绝。不测古怪、直觉、孤独或求认可需要。享受不同纸棋子走法无需特殊身份，也不拿谁的不适作娱乐；匹配不评足球技术、创作天赋。

title.en: An unexpected move with an ordinary invitation

paragraphs.en: A familiar round has become repetitive. You suggest a counter pattern that reverses one harmless rule and explain it before anyone plays. If the group prefers the old version, the suggestion can wait. The example is about shared playfulness, not imposing a surprise, embarrassing a friend or treating fictional inner voices and monsters as explanations for real thoughts or mental-health experiences.
paragraphs.zh: 熟悉一轮重复，你提棋子图样，反转一条无害规则，并先解释再玩。若大家喜欢旧版，可等。这是共同玩趣，不强加惊喜、不使朋友难堪、不用虚构内心声音、怪物解释现实思想或心理体验。

title.en: Playfulness beside six other contributions

paragraphs.en: Isagi revises after observing, Nagi finds a simple starting move and Reo explores a chosen role. Rin specifies the shared plan, Barou prepares with his own routine and Chigiri chooses a comfortable tempo. Bachira’s angle offers an agreed playful alternative. None is a rank in originality or social worth. A tie can mean several enjoyable contributions without assigning abandonment fears, hidden emotional needs or permanent labels.
paragraphs.zh: 洁观察后改，凪找简单首步，玲王探索自选角色；凛具体写共同计划，马狼按个人惯例准备，千切选舒服节奏。蜂乐给约好玩趣替代。不排原创性、价值；并列不派被弃恐惧、隐藏情感需要、永久标签。

title.en: A variation can remain only an idea

paragraphs.en: Not every playful idea needs to become a rule. A group may want familiarity, a shorter round or no further game today. You can enjoy imagining an alternative while accepting that choice. A higher count cannot prove unusual creativity or instinctive skill, and a lower count cannot show rigidity, isolation or a lack of joy. Shared consent matters more than making the session look spontaneous.
paragraphs.zh: 非每个趣味点子都需成规则，大家可要熟悉、短轮或今天不再玩。可享受想象同时接受选择。高计数不证明独特创意、本能技术，低计数不表示僵硬、孤立、没乐趣；共同同意比显得即兴重要。

title.en: Try a clearly optional variation

paragraphs.en: For one small paper round, offer an imaginative move and describe how people can decline it. If they agree, try it once and ask whether the game became more enjoyable or merely more complicated. Return to the earlier version if preferred. This explores a leisure choice, not your need for connection, psychological independence, athletic instincts or ability to overcome a difficult personal history.
paragraphs.zh: 给小纸回合提想象走法，说明怎样拒绝。同意则试一次，问更好玩还是只更复杂；可回旧版。这探索闲暇选择，不评联结需要、心理独立、运动本能或克服个人困难经历能力。

title.en: Nagi’s selected angle

paragraphs.en: Nagi’s name anchors a simple first attempt in this original tabletop bank. The angle does not measure laziness, natural genius, boredom or a hidden potential waiting to awaken. Beginning with one easy counter move can be a way to enjoy an optional hobby without committing to an elaborate sequence. It says nothing about how much effort you owe a group or how talented you are at sport.
paragraphs.zh: 凪在原创桌面题本对应简单首试，不测懒惰、天才、无聊或待觉醒潜力。从一个易走步开始，可让人无需承诺复杂序列就享受爱好，不说欠小组多少努力、不评体育天赋。

title.en: One turn before the whole system

paragraphs.en: Friends have designed a long tabletop sequence that takes a while to explain. You ask to try a single small part so everybody can see what it does. The group might enjoy that short round or decide to build more later. The useful feature is an approachable starting point, not effortless brilliance or proof that other people should supply your motivation and do the preparation for you.
paragraphs.zh: 朋友设计长序列、解释很久。你提先试一小部分，让大家见其作用。可享受短轮，也可后续再扩。有用处是好开始，不是毫不费力的天才，也不说别人应供动力、代准备。

title.en: Simplicity beside six other contributions

paragraphs.en: Isagi learns about the layout by observing, Bachira offers a playful variation and Reo chooses a contribution. Rin clarifies details, Barou keeps a personal preparation routine and Chigiri chooses a tempo. Nagi’s selected angle makes the first move small enough to try. These can support the same session without ranking effort or talent. A tie does not reveal dormant ability, emotional indifference or a fixed motivational type.
paragraphs.zh: 洁观察布局，蜂乐提趣味变式，玲王选贡献；凛澄清细节，马狼留个人准备惯例，千切选节奏。凪让首步小到能试。可支持同活动，不排努力、天赋；并列不揭潜力、情感冷漠、固定动力类型。

title.en: Simple does not mean ignoring shared work
title.zh: 简单不等于无视共同工作

paragraphs.en: A short version still needs the materials and agreement that make it playable. If a friend has offered to explain a rule, respect that contribution rather than assuming the game should arrive ready for you. A count cannot establish apathy or genius. A lower count does not mean overthinking, and a larger project can be enjoyable too when that is what participants actually want to make.
paragraphs.zh: 短版也需可玩的材料、约定。朋友自愿解释规则，可尊重其贡献，不默认游戏应替你全备好。次数不确立冷漠、天才，低计数不表示想太多；若大家真想做，大项目也可好玩。

title.en: Try a one-turn version

paragraphs.en: Take a voluntary paper-game idea and ask what a single playable turn would need. Set up only that part with willing friends, play once and decide whether to continue. Notice whether the smaller beginning made the activity easier to enjoy. This is feedback on scope, not a test of motivation, a claim about innate skill or an instruction to avoid effort in school, work or sport.
paragraphs.zh: 问自愿纸游戏一个可玩回合需什么，同愿意朋友只备这部分，玩一次再决定继续否。看小开头是否更好享受。这反馈范围，不测动力、不说天赋、不指导在学业、工作、运动中避努力。

title.en: Reo’s selected angle

paragraphs.en: Reo’s selected angle is choosing a contribution with room to change it by agreement. It does not measure versatility, wealth, dependence or your worth apart from a friend. You can enjoy arranging counters now and writing rules later without needing to mirror another person or prove independence. The match describes choices in a voluntary paper activity, not an account of how your close relationships work.
paragraphs.zh: 玲王角度是选贡献并留约好再改空间，不测多才、财富、依赖或离开朋友后的价值。可现在摆棋子、后写规则，不需模仿别人、证明独立。匹配描述自愿纸活动选择，不解释亲密关系运作。

title.en: A new part becomes interesting

paragraphs.en: After arranging the paper pitch, you become curious about writing an example rule. You ask whether somebody wants to swap contributions or whether you can take a new small part. The change follows an interest you have now. Nobody needs to lose a partner or be replaced as a person, and a different task does not make the earlier contribution less meaningful.
paragraphs.zh: 摆好纸球场后，你好奇写示例规则，问有谁想换贡献、能否接新小部分。变化跟随当前兴趣。无人需失去伙伴、被当人替换，换任务不使先前贡献失去意义。

title.en: Role choice beside six other contributions
title.zh: 角色选择与另六种贡献

paragraphs.en: Isagi observes and revises, Bachira offers play and Nagi begins simply. Rin defines details, Barou uses a personal routine and Chigiri chooses the tempo. Reo’s selected angle keeps the contribution a choice rather than a permanent assignment. Several angles can coexist without ranking versatility or relationship health. A tie does not show that you lack an identity, and no character count decides who you need beside you.
paragraphs.zh: 洁观察修改，蜂乐提玩趣，凪简单开始；凛定义细节，马狼用个人惯例，千切选节奏。玲王让贡献保持选择、不成永久指派。可共存，不排多才、关系健康；并列不说无身份，次数不决定需要谁陪伴。

title.en: Changing a task includes communicating it

paragraphs.en: A group can struggle if people silently leave parts they had agreed to finish. Say what you want to change and check which small commitments still need a handover. You can also decide to stop an optional activity. Your count cannot establish adaptability or unhealthy attachment, and a lower count does not mean inflexibility, isolation or an inability to contribute in more than one way.
paragraphs.zh: 默默丢下约好部分可使小组困难，可说想改什么，核哪些小承诺要交接，也能决定停可选活动。次数不确立适应力、不健康依恋；低计数不表示不灵活、孤立或只能单一贡献。

title.en: Try a clearly agreed role change
title.zh: 试一次清楚约好的角色变化

paragraphs.en: At a voluntary tabletop session, name one contribution you would like to try next and ask how to change parts without leaving an agreed task unclear. Try it for one round, then decide again. Notice whether the new part was enjoyable rather than treating flexibility as proof of worth. This is a hobby experiment, not advice about separation, identity, attachment or significant relationships.
paragraphs.zh: 自愿桌面活动中，说想试哪贡献，问怎样换才不使约好任务含糊。试一轮再选，注意是否有趣，不把灵活当价值证明。这试爱好，不建议分离、身份、依恋或重要关系。
